lead: A closure is an object of a compiler-synthesized class, so it renders as that class's name.
body: `rule:types/closure-literal` makes a literal an object with one field per capture, so `Core\Test::assertSame($f, $g)` over two `callable`s prints ``a `Script$fn0` `` and ``a `Script$fn1` `` — a name no rule owns. Keep a `callable` out of a case about how a value renders; the same goes for `Tag::Unset`, which no file-scope expression produces at all.
